description: We're Lost on Mars, a team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Campinas, Brazil. Our mission is to create an Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map to help future astronauts navigate Mars and identify essential survival resources.
summary:
Mars Explorer is an interactive planetary exploration platform that uses real NASA data to visualize Mars and plan safer surface exploration routes. It combines high-resolution terrain models, orbital imagery, geological and mineralogical information, thermal maps, and environmental data in a continuous 3D globe.

Users can select any locations on Mars, generate and compare routes using different safety profiles, and evaluate important mission parameters such as distance, travel time, oxygen consumption, radiation exposure, communication coverage, and return-to-base limits. The platform also includes a first-person exploration mode that simulates traversing the actual Martian terrain.

By transforming complex scientific datasets into an accessible exploration and planning tool, Mars Explorer helps people understand the challenges of human exploration while supporting educational activities and future mission planning research.
details:
Mars Explorer is an interactive 3D planetary exploration and route-planning platform designed to address the challenges of navigating and conducting scientific exploration on Mars.

The application integrates real planetary datasets from NASA, including topographic models, orbital imagery, thermal observations, geological maps, mineralogical information, and environmental measurements. These datasets are presented through a continuous 3D globe that allows users to explore Mars from a global perspective down to high-resolution surface details.

Its route-planning system allows users to select any starting point and multiple destinations on the Martian surface. Using an A* pathfinding algorithm, the platform generates and compares three route profiles: Fast, Balanced, and Safe. It evaluates terrain slope, surface roughness, obstacles, and mission constraints to estimate travel distance, duration, oxygen consumption, radiation exposure, communication coverage, sunlight conditions, and return-to-base limits.

The project also features a first-person simulation in which users can experience a planned Marswalk across real terrain data, with mission time, oxygen, radiation dose, and solar position evolving throughout the journey.

Additional scientific tools support geological exploration and the identification of potential locations for future human settlements.

The project was developed using JavaScript, Three.js, HTML, CSS, Node.js, and Vite, alongside scientific data services and publicly available planetary datasets.

Its main innovation is transforming complex scientific information into an accessible, interactive environment that connects planetary science, autonomous route planning, and human exploration scenarios.

Mars Explorer is an educational and research-oriented prototype intended to improve understanding of Martian surface conditions, demonstrate the challenges of human exploration, and support discussions about safer future exploration strategies.
